title: Micro-page compaction and heuristic prefetch scheduler for paged KV cache
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Problem: When serving large-context requests under oversubscription, the KV cache can fragment into many small resident pages and cause high GPU memory churn, excessive device->host swap, and tail-latency spikes. Existing slab allocators reduce some overhead but don't address cold-page compaction and prefetch ordering for continuous batching workloads.

Goal: Provide a practical implementation combining (1) background micro-page compaction to reduce fragmentation and reclaim contiguous GPU residency, and (2) a heuristic prefetch scheduler that orders KV page loads by expected near-term reuse (batch-aware) while respecting a tunable prefetch token budget and host PCIe bandwidth caps. The combination should reduce device swap frequency, lower 95/99th latency for token- heavy workloads, and limit CPU overhead to an acceptable percent of host capacity.

Scope: Implementation targets paged/blocked KV cache on Dedicated and Hosted runtime. This ticket covers design, prototype kernel integrations, unit/integration tests, and a limited canary rollout. It does not include on-prem packaging changes or new customer config surfaces beyond a small set of knobs (compaction window, prefetch_budget_tokens, prefetch_bandwidth_limit).
acceptance_criteria:
1) End-to-end integration that compacts fragmented KV pages into contiguous residency blocks without requiring model reloads.
2) Prefetch scheduler orders page loads to keep active batch latencies within SLO for synthetic workloads with >60% KV miss rates.
3) End-to-end p95 latency reduction >= 20% and p99 reduction >= 15% on KV-heavy benchmarks vs current baseline (same model/runtime).
4) CPU overhead for compaction/prefetch threads stays <5% of one host core under representative load.
5) Feature gated and disabled by default; documented knobs and telemetry.
6) Tests: unit tests for compaction correctness, integration with simulated oversubscription, and a canary run with production-like traces.
benchmarks: Local synthetic: seq-len mix [64,2048], batch sizes [1,8,32], kv-miss 40/60/80 -> baseline vs compaction+prefetch
Staging trace replay: 72h production trace scaled to 2x QPS -> observe p50/p95/p99 and device swap counts
PCIe bandwidth monitor: confirm prefetch caps reduce host->device traffic spikes
implementation_notes:
Core idea: expose micro-pages (4-32KB logical units) tiled into larger residency segments. Compaction agent coalesces adjacent live micro-pages into a contiguous segment when fragmentation ratio > threshold and when GPU IO budget allows. Prefetch scheduler observes the continuous batching queue: it scores missing micro-pages by a combination of (a) recency within batch, (b) estimated position in KV access sequence (prefix vs suffix), and (c) cross-request reuse probability learned from short-term access histogram. Prefetch launches use batched DMA where possible to amortize PCIe setup.

Memory model adjustments: support 'soft-pinned' staging buffers on host (page-locked) with a bounded pool per GPU to avoid host OOM. Integrate with existing slab metadata but keep compaction decisions independent of allocator eviction logic to avoid cycles. Provide a 'dry-run' mode where compaction only simulates coalescing to collect metrics before committing.

Trade-offs considered: heavier compaction reduces fragmentation but can increase short-term device->host traffic; therefore we prioritize compaction during low-throughput windows and when a contiguous free range provides immediate benefit (e.g., for next batch predicted casts). A learning rate parameter governs histogram decay to avoid chasing noisy access patterns.
testing_plan:
Unit: compaction correctness under synthetic layouts, eviction interplay tests, race-condition fuzzing.
Integration: replay of 48-hour production traces with stress variations (spike, sustained oversubscribe).
Performance: End-to-end benchmarks vs baseline for 5 models (2 encoder-decoder, 3 decoder-only) across GPUs (A100-40GB, H100-80GB) with oversubscription factors 1.5x and 3x.
Canary: 2-week canary in staging fleet with gradual traffic ramp and rollback on error budget breach or increased device_swap_count beyond threshold.
rollout_and_migration: Feature gated under runtime flag 'kv.micro_compaction_v1' and 'kv.prefetch_v1'. Default off for existing Dedicated customers. For Dedicated customers who opt-in, provide migration doc that recommends gradual enabling and monitoring steps. If compaction runs detect heavy fragmentation but limited benefit, fall back to noop and emit advisory metric. Provide a one-click rollback via console rollout policies.
risks_and_mitigation:
Risk: compaction causing unexpected latency spikes during high QPS. Mitigation: compaction runs are preemptible and throttle by observed p95 latency; enable dry-run telemetry to validate heuristics before commit.
Risk: prefetch overloading PCIe and starving other I/O. Mitigation: enforce prefetch_bandwidth_limit and adaptive budget reduction when IO contention metrics rise.
Risk: incorrect coalescing interacting with allocator -> potential memory corruption. Mitigation: strict invariants + unit tests + canary with memory sanitizer builds.
follow_up_tasks: Add lightweight online model to predict reuse probability (separate ticket)
Expose safe tuning UI in Console with suggested defaults per workload
Investigate HBM-aware compaction policies for multi-GPU NUMA setups
